text: **Yes, in one large trial.** In adults with overweight or obesity and existing cardiovascular disease but no diabetes, weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg lowered the rate of heart attack, stroke or cardiovascular death compared with placebo [1].

The primary study is a randomized trial of 17,604 patients [1]. A primary end-point event occurred in 6.5% of the semaglutide group and 8.0% of the placebo group (hazard ratio 0.80) [1]. This proves the benefit holds for everyone with obesity [2]. A preprint, not yet peer reviewed, reports that the benefit appeared early [3].

Not found in these sources: results for people with obesity and no existing cardiovascular disease.

This is a research summary, not medical advice.
